claims.claim: Martin says he can easily write that a character said something in a Dornish accent even though no Dornish accent exists, leaving the audiobook reader to invent one.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, History of Westeros interview (recorded 2022-08-18)
claims.quote: I can easily write so and so said this in a Dornish accent
claims.page: transcript, section on Roy Dotrice and audiobooks

claims.claim: Martin says he does not think he has ever used the word soul in A Song of Ice and Fire.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, History of Westeros interview (recorded 2022-08-18)
claims.quote: I don’t think I’ve ever used that word
claims.page: transcript, listener question about the soul

claims.claim: Martin says that where resonances between his histories and his main series arise he tries to veer away from them so as not to feel he is repeating himself.
claims.source: George R.R. Martin, History of Westeros interview (recorded 2022-08-18)
claims.quote: I try to veer away from that

claims.claim: Elio García says The World of Ice and Fire was written by a maester in the Citadel from information he had compiled without having witnessed the events.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr., ShadowDance interview (2017-10-16)
claims.quote: It was written by a maester in the Citadel based on information that he had
claims.page: interview, question on the maester frame

claims.claim: García says the maester frame lets the maester be wrong because he is not a personal witness.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr., ShadowDance interview (2017-10-16)
claims.quote: the maester can be wrong because he’s not a personal witness
claims.page: interview, question on the maester frame

claims.claim: García says Yandel is sometimes deliberately wrong in The World of Ice and Fire and that they played up how wrong he was.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr., ShadowDance interview (2017-10-16)
claims.quote: our master Yandel is just wrong
claims.page: interview, question on mistakes in the book

claims.claim: Linda Antonsson says they invented small things such as book titles and maesters for the text to reference.
claims.quote: we invented small things like book titles, or maesters, to reference
claims.page: interview, question on the ratio of Martin's input

claims.claim: Antonsson says Martin wrote over 200,000 words for the Targaryen material of The World of Ice and Fire alone.
claims.quote: he wrote over 200,000 words for the Targaryen material only
claims.page: interview, question on the ratio of Martin's input

claims.claim: Antonsson says The World of Ice and Fire ended up around 180,000 words by plan.
claims.quote: The book itself ended up around 180,000 words by plan
claims.page: interview, question on the ratio of Martin's input

claims.claim: García says writing history and geography is not at all the same as creating the interweaving plots of the novels.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr., ShadowDance interview (2017-10-16)
claims.quote: Writing history and geography is not at all the same

claims.claim: García says the Ironborn section of The World of Ice and Fire has serious continuity errors because Martin wrote it last and did not cross-check it against the earlier kingdoms.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr., ShadowDance interview (2017-10-16)
claims.quote: there are serious continuity errors between this section and all the others
claims.page: interview, question on mistakes in the book

claims.claim: Antonsson says the concept of a maester writing The World of Ice and Fire was their suggestion, not Martin's.
claims.source: Linda Antonsson, La Garde de Nuit interview (recorded Worldcon Dublin 2019, published 2020-03-25)
claims.quote: the concept of the book, the idea that there would be a maester writing it
claims.page: transcript, About The World of Ice and Fire

claims.claim: Antonsson says their maester frame was inspired in part by Martin's idea of a guidebook written by a traveller who would not have perfect knowledge.
claims.source: Linda Antonsson, La Garde de Nuit interview (published 2020-03-25)
claims.quote: a guidebook written by a traveler in the world so that he wouldn’t have a perfect knowledge
claims.page: transcript, About The World of Ice and Fire

claims.claim: Antonsson says the preface with the scratched-out names was something they particularly wanted in the book.
claims.source: Linda Antonsson, La Garde de Nuit interview (published 2020-03-25)
claims.quote: the preface with the scratched-out names
claims.page: transcript, About The World of Ice and Fire

claims.claim: García says Yandel hides certain ugly details because he wants the book to spread and is writing about powerful living people.
claims.source: Elio M. García Jr., La Garde de Nuit interview (published 2020-03-25)
claims.quote: he has to hide certain details, ugly details

verdicts.trueWording: cuz of course I can easily write so and so said this in a Dornish accent. There's no Dornish accent. So Roy would have to make it up
verdicts.note: Live page fetched raw with a browser UA (HTTP 200). Quote is word for word in the Roy Dotrice/audiobook passage; the page also carries 'There's no Dornish accent' and 'So Roy would have to make it up and say I will make that a Spanish accent', supporting both remaining limbs.

verdicts.trueWording: George: Yes. I don't think I've ever used that word, but...
verdicts.note: Raw live page. Verbatim, in answer to the listener question 'do individuals have, or believe in the soul?' set explicitly 'in your world of A Song of Ice and Fire'; Aziz confirms 'No, you haven't'. Every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Certain similarities are inevitable. If anything, I try to veer away from that, cuz I don't wanna feel like I'm repeating myself.
verdicts.note: Raw live page, Parallel Lives exchange. Verbatim; the question is about parallels between the histories (Fire and Blood) and the main-series characters, and Martin adds 'there are certain resonances in history'. Both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: It was written by a maester in the Citadel based on information that he had but of course he didn't witness those things and he's compiled together
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture (id_) fetched, HTTP 200. Verbatim; speaker confirmed as Elio (nearest preceding speaker tag). The 'compiled / did not witness' limb is on the page in the same sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: So you have a maester writing it and the maester can be wrong because he's not a personal witness.
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture. Verbatim, Elio speaking, in the passage explaining the benefit of the maester frame (George not 'pinned down to some facts').

verdicts.trueWording: Some of it was intentional, because our master Yandel is just wrong ... And sometimes we even played up a lot with how wrong he was
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture. Verbatim ('our master Yandel' is the page's own wording, apparently for maester); Elio speaking. Both limbs -- deliberate wrongness and playing it up -- are on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: So we didn't really invent anything - we invented small things like book titles, or maesters, to reference.
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture. Verbatim; speaker confirmed as Linda, in the answer about the ratio of Martin's input.

verdicts.trueWording: cause he wrote over 200,000 words for the Targaryen material only
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture. Verbatim, Linda speaking, about the TWOIAF sidebars 'that turned into long novellas'.

verdicts.trueWording: The book itself ended up around 180,000 words by plan.
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture. Verbatim, Linda speaking, immediately after the 200,000-word sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: Writing history and geography is not at all the same as creating these huge interweaving plots that are in the novels.
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture. Verbatim; nearest preceding speaker tag is Elio. The claim's 'interweaving plots of the novels' matches the page's 'huge interweaving plots that are in the novels'.

verdicts.trueWording: he did the Ironborn section ... he had the time to go back and cross-check ... but he didn't do it with the Ironborn. So there are serious continuity errors between this section and all the others
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture, Elio speaking. Quote verbatim; the 'wrote it last' limb ('towards the end of this process, where we really already had to have the manuscript finalized') and the 'no cross-check against earlier kingdoms' limb are both explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: And also the concept of the book, the idea that there would be a maester writing it. That was also our suggestion from early on, inspired in part of George that has this idea
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture (25 mars 2020 publication date confirmed on the page); speaker confirmed as Linda. The quotation is verbatim and 'our suggestion from early on' is on the page, but the page does not say the concept was not Martin's -- it says the suggestion was theirs *inspired in part* by George's own idea of a fallible in-world guidebook narrator. The exclusive negation is the claim's addition.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: not Martin's -- the page qualifies it as 'inspired in part of George that has this idea'

verdicts.trueWording: inspired in part of George that has this idea, that it is a guidebook written by a traveler in the world so that he wouldn't have a perfect knowledge
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture, Linda speaking. Verbatim (page spells 'traveler'); the 'inspired in part by Martin's idea' limb is the page's own clause.

verdicts.trueWording: the introduction, the preface with the scratched-out names and so on, that something we really wanted to have
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture, Linda speaking. Quote verbatim; 'particularly wanted' matches the page's 'that something we really wanted to have'.

verdicts.trueWording: he wants the book to spread, and he has to hide certain details, ugly details
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture, Elio speaking about Yandel. Verbatim; the 'powerful living people' limb is on the page: 'when he's writing about very powerful people like Tywin Lannister, he needs to be careful', with Yandel described as 'a contemporary figure of the story'.
